newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-ENGLAND RE-WRITE RECORD BOOKS AS RUN CONTINUES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLAND RE-WRITE RECORD BOOKS AS RUN CONTINUES.

text.p: England can look forward to proving against world champions Brazil in Paris on Tuesday just how far they have progressed under coach Glenn Hoddle.
Their spirits were sky-high as they flew to Paris on Sunday after stretching their winning run to six matches with a 1-0 victory over France in the Tournoi de France on Saturday night.
And at the Parc des Princes against Brazil they can achieve something they have not done since 1966 -- win seven successive internationals.

The last time an England team did that was between February and the beginning of July 1966 when they won seven warm-up games just before the start of the World Cup finals in which they were crowned world champions.
It was a night when other records also fell. England became the first team since Bulgaria in December 1993 to beat France at home -- and they also won their first match in France for 48 years.

It was the first time in England's 125-year soccer history they had gone six away matches without conceding a goal. Their previous best run before this current sequence was five matches between July 1966 and February 1968.
The run started in October 1995 when they drew 0-0 in Norway and has continued with wins over China (3-0), Moldova (3-0), Georgia (2-0), Poland (2-0), Italy (2-0) and Saturday's win over France.
Discounting the goal they conceded in their abandoned match against Ireland in Dublin in February 1995, the last team to score against England away from home was San Marino in November 1993.
Skipper Alan Shearer, who scored the only goal five minutes from time to take his personal tally to 11 goals in his last 11 internationals, summed up the mood in the squad afterwards.

"Our confidence is sky-high right now. We don't really want to use up all our luck now because you need some of that to win World Cups. But we feel we are at the top of the mountain, although we still have to go and prove ourselves against the best.

"When you're at at the top, there is only one way to fall. We are not getting carried away because we haven't achieved anything yet. But we feel as though we have made progress and are going in the right direction."
England have only lost twice in open play in their last 34 internationals -- not counting the penalty shootout defeat to Germany in last summer's Euro'96 semifinals.

Looking back a year, Shearer added: "We may have made a lot of progress under Glenn Hoddle in the last year, but we were a good team a year ago, and only failed on penalties to reach the European final. I think we are improving all the time."
Frank LeBouef, who plays his league football in England with Chelsea and was on the French substitute's bench on Saturday, agreed.

"They have showed just how far they have come in the last year under Hoddle. They are more assured and professional. They hold the ball more, they don't just try to put it anywhere. They have learnt a lot and look like a real threat to anyone," he said.
Hoddle, who was delighted to win in France where he spent time as a player in the 1980s with Monaco, retained his usual level-headedness after a very physical, hard-fought win.

"We knew it was going to be harder than the match against Italy and I am delighted we've got six wins in a row. It means we are finding the right balance -- keeping clean sheets and scoring at the other end. We are looking for that cutting edge and, if you have that, you're in with a good chance in football matches."
The only thing that disappointed England was the bizarre first-half booking for David Beckham, who was shown the yellow card by the referee for refusing to be carried off on a stretcher.
He needed treatment after a crunching tackle from Patrick Vieira, and hobbled off rather than be carried off.
The referee, Said Belgola of Morocco, called for the stretcher without consultation with the England medics -- then booked Beckham for dissent when he refused to get on it.
Despite the absurdity of the decision, the booking was Beckham's second of the tournament and means he is suspended from playing against Brazil.
"It is every player's dream to play against them," said Beckham afterwards, "and I've been denied by a very strange decision."
"You have to learn from the negative as well as the positive," said Hoddle afterwards.
